_purpose: The checked-in rules for what reaches main (LAN-523, ADR 0041). There are no pull requests: a branch passes every check locally and reaches main in one push. This file says how much attention that push needs, judged from the branch's real diff against origin/main. `reviewRequired` paths need one code-reviewer pass at the branch's final head before the push; any other branch is pushed with no review. `ownerOnly` paths are pushed by Brian alone. Read by scripts/merge/gate.mjs, the mission gate and review-contract generation; `requiredChecks` is read by .github/workflows/deploy.yml.
_requiredChecksNote: The job `name:` values in .github/workflows/ci.yml. `deploy.yml` refuses any commit on which these are not green, so with no pull requests this list is the only gate between a push and production. Renaming a job in ci.yml without updating this list fails a test instead of silently emptying the gate.

_reviewRequiredNote: A match means one code-reviewer pass at the branch's final head before it is pushed to main. Judged from the real diff — a rename on both its names. Everything not listed here is pushed without review.

ownerOnly.reason: The approved packet itself. Its landing on main IS Brian's approval of that exact packet version; no agent pushes it. Mission prose and walkthrough records beside it are ordinary documentation.

_ownerOnlyNote: A match means Brian pushes the branch himself.
_visualSurfacesNote: The coherence tripwire: a receipt claiming nonvisual work is refused when the diff touches any of these, so ADR 0020's live visual review cannot be skipped by mislabelling. Visual work still needs Brian's visual approval at the exact head before the push.

reviewContract._purpose: The path classifiers that generate a package review contract in scripts/mission/lib/review-contract.mjs. They decide which capabilities and jobs an invocation must carry; the Mission Lead may add a diagnostic question but may never remove what these produce.
reviewContract._sensitiveSurfacesNote: Auth, authorization, schema, privileged clients, public token issuance, production procedure and workflow surfaces. A non-empty intersection always requires a fresh reviewer.
reviewContract._databaseSurfacesNote: Behaviour whose acceptance depends on rows. A non-empty intersection requires the database and database-reset-seed capabilities and live job evidence; static reasoning cannot clear it.
reviewContract._publicSurfacesNote: Token and answer flows reachable without a session. They require a public browser context and the scanner and reload negative jobs.
reviewContract._transportSurfacesNote: The provider/local transport seam. Changing it requires the seam capability so delivery is exercised against the local transport rather than reasoned about.
reviewContract._evidenceSurfacesNote: Seed and fixture sources. A change here alters what every later proof is measured against, so it is review-affecting even when no component changed; deterministic clearance is refused.
